review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

9:1.sourceText: Ὁ δὲ Σαῦλος ἔτι ἐμπνέων ἀπειλῆς καὶ φόνου εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς τοῦ Κυρίου, προσελθὼν τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ
9:1.targetText: Meanwhile, Saul was still breathing out murderous threats against the disciples of the Lord. He approached the high priest

groups.note: BSB renders the δέ that returns to Saul's story (8:3) as Meanwhile.
The participle ἐμπνέων ("breathing") is rendered as a finite verb.
ἀπειλῆς καὶ φόνου ("threat and murder") is rendered murderous threats.
The participle προσελθών ("having approached") is rendered as a new sentence.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB joins threat and murder as murderous threats; this καί has no separate word.

9:2.sourceText: ᾐτήσατο παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐπιστολὰς εἰς Δαμασκὸν πρὸς τὰς συναγωγάς, ὅπως ἐάν τινας εὕρῃ τῆς Ὁδοῦ ὄντας, ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας, δεδεμένους ἀγάγῃ εἰς Ἱερουσαλήμ.
9:2.targetText: and requested letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any men or women belonging to the Way, he could bring them as prisoners to Jerusalem.

groups.note: εἰς Δαμασκόν ("to Damascus") is rendered in Damascus, locating the synagogues.
ὄντας ("being") with the genitive is rendered belonging to.
After "if he found any", καί is rendered or.
The participle δεδεμένους ("bound") is rendered as prisoners.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render παρ’ αὐτοῦ ("from him"); the high priest is named in 9:1.
The τε of τε καί ("both … and") is rendered only by the following or.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle προσελθών (9:1), rendered He approached, to the main verb requested.
English supplies the object of bring; the Greek has only the participle δεδεμένους.

9:3.sourceText: Ἐν δὲ τῷ πορεύεσθαι ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐγγίζειν τῇ Δαμασκῷ, ἐξαίφνης τε αὐτὸν περιήστραψεν φῶς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ,
9:3.targetText: As Saul drew near to Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.

groups.note: The articular infinitive τῷ πορεύεσθαι ("the traveling") is rendered his journey.
The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name.
BSB turns the two clauses joined by τε into "As …, …".

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves the narrative formula ἐγένετο ("it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:4.sourceText: καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἤκουσεν φωνὴν λέγουσαν αὐτῷ Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;
9:4.targetText: He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle πεσών, rendered He fell, to the main verb heard.

9:5.sourceText: εἶπεν δέ Τίς εἶ, Κύριε; ὁ δέ Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις·
9:5.targetText: “Who are You, Lord?” Saul asked.  “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,” He replied.

groups.note: εἶπεν is understood again with ὁ δέ ("and he"); BSB renders it asked and then replied.
The article ὁ is used as a pronoun ("he").

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending of εἶπεν.

9:6.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ λαληθήσεταί σοι ὅ τί σε δεῖ ποιεῖν.
9:6.targetText: “Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”

groups.note: ἀλλά ("but") turning to the command is rendered Now.
The dative σοι ("to you") becomes the subject of the passive in English.
ὅ τι ("whatever") together supply what.

9:7.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἄνδρες οἱ συνοδεύοντες αὐτῷ εἱστήκεισαν ἐνεοί, ἀκούοντες μὲν τῆς φωνῆς, μηδένα δὲ θεωροῦντες.
9:7.targetText: The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless. They heard the voice but did not see anyone.

groups.note: The article with the participle συνοδεύοντες ("those traveling with") is rendered traveling with.
The pronoun αὐτῷ ("him") is rendered by the name.
The participle ἀκούοντες ("hearing") is rendered as a new sentence.
μηδένα ("no one") is rendered not … anyone.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The particle μέν, answered by δέ (but), has no English counterpart.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds there; εἱστήκεισαν means only stood.

9:8.sourceText: ἠγέρθη δὲ Σαῦλος ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, ἀνεῳγμένων δὲ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτοῦ οὐδὲν ἔβλεπεν· χειραγωγοῦντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἰσήγαγον εἰς Δαμασκόν.
9:8.targetText: Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could not see a thing. So they led him by the hand into Damascus.

groups.note: The passive genitive absolute ἀνεῳγμένων ("having been opened") is rendered as an active when-clause.
οὐδέν ("nothing") is rendered not … a thing.
The participle χειραγωγοῦντες ("leading by the hand") is rendered by the hand.
εἰσήγαγον ("they brought in") is rendered led … into, with into for εἰς.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:9.sourceText: καὶ ἦν ἡμέρας τρεῖς μὴ βλέπων, καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲ ἔπιεν.
9:9.targetText: For three days he was without sight, and he did not eat or drink anything.

groups.note: μὴ βλέπων ("not seeing") is rendered without sight.
οὐδέ ("nor") after the negative is rendered or.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for eat and drink; the Greek has none.

9:10.sourceText: Ἦν δέ τις μαθητὴς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὀνόματι Ἀνανίας, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν ὁράματι ὁ Κύριος Ἀνανία. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ, Κύριε.
9:10.targetText: In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision, “Ananias!”  “Here I am, Lord,” he answered.

groups.note: The article ὁ is used as a pronoun ("he").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB opens the new scene without rendering δέ.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ ("behold, I") has no verb.

9:11.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν Ἀναστὰς πορεύθητι ἐπὶ τὴν ῥύμην τὴν καλουμένην Εὐθεῖαν καὶ ζήτησον ἐν οἰκίᾳ Ἰούδα Σαῦλον ὀνόματι Ταρσέα· ἰδοὺ γὰρ προσεύχεται,
9:11.targetText: “Get up!” the Lord told him. “Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.

groups.note: πρὸς αὐτόν ("to him") is rendered as the object of told.
BSB makes the house the destination; ἐπί ("to") the street is rendered to.
BSB places the house on the street; ἐν ("in") is rendered on.
Ταρσέα ("a Tarsian") is rendered a man from Tarsus.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB gives the name Straight Street and has no word for τὴν καλουμένην ("the one called").
BSB leaves ἰδού ("behold") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb of speaking; the Greek clause ὁ δὲ Κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν has none.

9:12.sourceText: καὶ εἶδεν ἄνδρα Ἀνανίαν ὀνόματι εἰσελθόντα καὶ ἐπιθέντα αὐτῷ χεῖρας, ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃ.
9:12.targetText: In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come and place his hands on him to restore his sight.”

groups.note: ἀναβλέψῃ ("he may see again") is rendered to restore his sight.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with extra words here; N1904 does not say in a vision.
English supplies the possessive; N1904 has no article or pronoun with hands, and BSB's Greek text has extra words in this verse.

9:13.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ Ἀνανίας Κύριε, ἤκουσα ἀπὸ πολλῶν περὶ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς τούτου, ὅσα κακὰ τοῖς ἁγίοις σου ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἱερουσαλήμ·
9:13.targetText: But Ananias answered, “Lord, many people have told me about this man and all the harm he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem.

groups.note: ἤκουσα ("I heard") from many is rendered many people have told me.
ὅσα κακά ("how many evils") is rendered all the harm.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes the many the subject of have told me, so ἀπό ("from") has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the second object of about; the Greek ὅσα clause has no connective.

9:14.sourceText: καὶ ὧδε ἔχει ἐξουσίαν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων δῆσαι πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομά σου.
9:14.targetText: And now he is here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on Your name.”

groups.note: ἔχει ("he has") authority is rendered he is … with authority.
The article with the participle ἐπικαλουμένους ("those calling on") is rendered who call on.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds now; the Greek has only ὧδε ("here").

9:15.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Κύριος Πορεύου, ὅτι σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς ἐστίν μοι οὗτος τοῦ βαστάσαι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐνώπιον ἐθνῶν τε καὶ βασιλέων υἱῶν τε Ἰσραήλ·
9:15.targetText: “Go!” said the Lord. “This man is My chosen instrument to carry My name before the Gentiles and their kings, and before the people of Israel.

groups.note: ἐκλογῆς ("of choice") is rendered chosen.
The dative μοι ("to me") is rendered My.
The articular infinitive τοῦ βαστάσαι expresses purpose.
The one ἐνώπιον governs Gentiles, kings and Israel; BSB repeats before.
υἱῶν ("sons") of Israel is rendered the people of Israel.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB does not render πρὸς αὐτόν ("to him") after said.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves ὅτι ("for") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The τε of τε καί ("both … and") is rendered only by the following and.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies their; the Greek has kings alone.

9:16.sourceText: ἐγὼ γὰρ ὑποδείξω αὐτῷ ὅσα δεῖ αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματός μου παθεῖν.
9:16.targetText: I will show him how much he must suffer for My name.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render γάρ ("for") here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:17.sourceText: Ἀπῆλθεν δὲ Ἀνανίας καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, καὶ ἐπιθεὶς ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ὁ Κύριος ἀπέσταλκέν με, Ἰησοῦς ὁ ὀφθείς σοι ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ᾗ ἤρχου, ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃς καὶ πλησθῇς Πνεύματος Ἁγίου.
9:17.targetText: So Ananias went to the house, and when he arrived, he placed his hands on Saul. “Brother Saul,” he said, “the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

groups.note: εἰσῆλθεν ("he entered") is rendered arrived.
εἰς belongs with εἰσῆλθεν; BSB puts to the house after went.
BSB turns the two clauses joined by καί into "when …, …".
The participle ἐπιθείς ("having placed") is rendered as a finite verb.
The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name.
The article τάς serves as the possessive.
The article with the participle ὀφθείς ("the one who appeared") is rendered who appeared.
The relative ᾗ ("by which") is rendered as.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds here; the Greek has only ἤρχου ("you were coming").

9:18.sourceText: καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέπεσαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ὡς λεπίδες, ἀνέβλεψέν τε, καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐβαπτίσθη,
9:18.targetText: At that instant, something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and his sight was restored. He got up and was baptized,

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered by the name.
ἀνέβλεψεν ("he saw again") is rendered his sight was restored.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for fell; the Greek says only that like scales fell.
English joins the participle ἀναστάς, rendered He got up, to the main verb baptized.

9:19.sourceText: καὶ λαβὼν τροφὴν ἐνίσχυσεν. Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐν Δαμασκῷ μαθητῶν ἡμέρας τινὰς,
9:19.targetText: and after taking some food, he regained his strength. And he spent several days with the disciples in Damascus.

groups.note: ἐγένετο ("he was") with the days is rendered he spent.

9:20.sourceText: καὶ εὐθέως ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ἐκήρυσσεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν, ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ.
9:20.targetText: Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, declaring, “He is the Son of God.”

groups.note: The imperfect ἐκήρυσσεν ("he was proclaiming") is rendered began to proclaim.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts the verse without rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ὅτι introduces what Saul proclaimed; BSB gives it as a direct quotation.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending of ἐκήρυσσεν.
English supplies a verb of saying to introduce the quotation.

9:21.sourceText: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες καὶ ἔλεγον Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ πορθήσας εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομα τοῦτο, καὶ ὧδε εἰς τοῦτο ἐληλύθει, ἵνα δεδεμένους αὐτοὺς ἀγάγῃ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς;
9:21.targetText: All who heard him were astounded and asked, “Isn’t this the man who wreaked havoc in Jerusalem on those who call on this name? And hasn’t he come here to take them as prisoners to the chief priests?”

groups.note: The article with the participle ἀκούοντες ("those hearing") is rendered who heard.
Οὐχ … ἐστιν ("is not") together form the contraction.
The article with the participle πορθήσας ("the one who ravaged") is rendered the man who wreaked havoc on.
The article with the participle ἐπικαλουμένους ("those calling on") is rendered those who call on.
The pluperfect ἐληλύθει ("he had come") is rendered hasn't he come, carrying on the negative question begun with Οὐχ.
The participle δεδεμένους ("bound") is rendered as prisoners.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render εἰς τοῦτο ("for this purpose"); the purpose is given by to take.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for heard.

9:22.sourceText: Σαῦλος δὲ μᾶλλον ἐνεδυναμοῦτο καὶ συνέχυννεν Ἰουδαίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν Δαμασκῷ, συμβιβάζων ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός.
9:22.targetText: But Saul was empowered all the more, and he confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.

groups.note: The article with the participle κατοικοῦντας ("those living") gives the Jews living.
οὗτος ("this one") is rendered by the name Jesus.

9:23.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦντο ἡμέραι ἱκαναί, συνεβουλεύσαντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν·
9:23.targetText: After many days had passed, the Jews conspired to kill him,

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

9:24.sourceText: ἐγνώσθη δὲ τῷ Σαύλῳ ἡ ἐπιβουλὴ αὐτῶν. παρετηροῦντο δὲ καὶ τὰς πύλας ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτὸς ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀνέλωσιν·
9:24.targetText: but Saul learned of their plot. Day and night they watched the city gates in order to kill him.

groups.note: The passive ἐγνώσθη ("was made known") to Saul is rendered Saul learned of.
ὅπως ("so that") is rendered in order to.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves δέ unrendered.
καί ("also") is not separately expressed.

9:25.sourceText: λαβόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς διὰ τοῦ τείχους καθῆκαν αὐτὸν χαλάσαντες ἐν σπυρίδι.
9:25.targetText: One night, however, his disciples took him and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall.

groups.note: νυκτός ("by night") is rendered One night.
καθῆκαν ("let down") and χαλάσαντες ("lowering") are rendered by the one verb lowered.
The one object αὐτόν serves λαβόντες and καθῆκαν; BSB gives him with both.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle λαβόντες, rendered took, to the main verb lowered.
BSB adds a window; the Greek says only through the wall.

9:26.sourceText: Παραγενόμενος δὲ εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπείραζεν κολλᾶσθαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς· καὶ πάντες ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτόν, μὴ πιστεύοντες ὅτι ἐστὶν μαθητής.

groups.note: The participle παραγενόμενος ("having arrived") is rendered as a when-clause.
καί joins a contrasting clause and is rendered but.

9:27.sourceText: Βαρνάβας δὲ ἐπιλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους, καὶ διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶδεν τὸν Κύριον καὶ ὅτι ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ, καὶ πῶς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ἐπαρρησιάσατο ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ.
9:27.targetText: Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and described how Saul had seen the Lord, who spoke to him on the road to Damascus, and how Saul had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus.

groups.note: BSB turns καὶ ὅτι ("and that") He spoke into a relative clause, who spoke.

BSB does not render αὐτοῖς ("to them") after described.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.
English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

9:28.sourceText: καὶ ἦν μετ’ αὐτῶν εἰσπορευόμενος καὶ ἐκπορευόμενος εἰς Ἱερουσαλήμ, παρρησιαζόμενος ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου,

9:30.sourceText: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ κατήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάριαν καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν εἰς Ταρσόν.

9:33.sourceText: εὗρεν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπόν τινα ὀνόματι Αἰνέαν ἐξ ἐτῶν ὀκτὼ κατακείμενον ἐπὶ κραβάττου, ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος.
